name: Driving Licence
department: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways — Parivahan/Sarathi
summary: Apply for a Learner's Licence followed by a Permanent Driving Licence through the state Regional Transport Office (RTO), managed via the national Sarathi/Parivahan platform.
eligibility: Minimum age 18 for a licence to drive a motor car or motorcycle with gear (16 for gearless two-wheelers up to 50cc, with parental consent)
Must pass a learner's test and, after 30 days, a driving test at the RTO
documents: Proof of age (birth certificate, PAN, or Aadhaar)
Proof of address (Aadhaar, utility bill, rent agreement)
Medical certificate (Form 1A) for certain vehicle classes or applicants above 40/50
fee: State-specific; illustrative RTO fees are roughly ₹200 for a Learner's Licence and ₹200-300 for a Permanent Licence, plus test and smart-card fees. Check your state RTO for exact charges.
process: Register on the Sarathi Parivahan portal and select your state RTO
Apply for and pass the online Learner's Licence (LL) test
Download the LL, valid for 6 months
After a minimum 30-day gap, apply for the Permanent Licence and book a driving test slot
Pass the in-person driving test at the RTO
Receive the DL by post or download the e-DL

faq.question: Can I apply for a driving licence without a learner's licence?
faq.answer: No. A Learner's Licence (LL) is mandatory and must be held for at least 30 days before you can appear for the Permanent Licence driving test.

faq.question: Is the driving licence fee the same across states?
faq.answer: No — RTO fees are set at the state level and vary. Always confirm the current fee on your state's Sarathi/RTO page before applying.
